analysis.market_overview: Italy has 3.4 million freelancers with a VAT number, of which 1.9 million are in the flat-rate regime (regime forfettario) [S3]. 44% of flat-rate freelancers already use an invoicing app, and the average price paid is 7.20 euros per month [S3]. E-invoicing via the SdI became mandatory for all flat-rate freelancers on 1 January 2024, whatever their revenue [S2, S17]. New flat-rate registrations are steady: 233,511 in 2024 [S16] and 242,529 in 2025, 48.5% of new VAT numbers and +3.9% on 2024 [S15]. The market is crowded and price-led. Fatture in Cloud is the leader, with a flat-rate offer at 4 euros per month in the first year (48 euros + VAT), rising to 8 euros per month (96 euros + VAT) afterwards [S6]. Other apps start at about 1 to 5 euros per month [S8, S9, S10]. The Agenzia delle Entrate offers free tools [S14]. Fiscozen sells an online accountant service from 49.90 euros per month [S11]. Tax-estimate and F24 features already exist in the flat-rate niche [S12, S13]. Fakturo's planned price is 9 euros per month or 90 euros per year [S1].

competitors.name: Fatture in Cloud
competitors.positioning: Market leader with broad features for small businesses and freelancers. It has a dedicated flat-rate plan with e-invoicing, turnover-limit monitoring and a flat-rate tax guide. Plans renew automatically and are paid yearly, with a 31-day free trial. The document gives 4 to 30 euros per month; the web shows 4 euros per month in the first year for new flat-rate customers, then 8 euros per month, and plans up to 51 euros per month.

competitors.name: Agenzia delle Entrate free tools
competitors.positioning: Free official tools: a web procedure, a PC software and the FatturAE app, which can prepare and transmit e-invoices to the SdI. The document describes them as basic invoicing with no tax estimate. Non-app users mostly rely on them.

competitors.name: Fattura24
competitors.positioning: E-invoicing app for professionals, with simplified management and a 30-day trial.

competitors.name: Aruba Fatturazione Elettronica
competitors.positioning: Easy to use and pitched at flat-rate freelancers. It has a very low entry price (1 euro + VAT for the first 3 months). The full package costs 134.60 euros + VAT per year at renewal.

competitors.name: FatturaElettronica APP
competitors.positioning: E-invoicing app for freelancers and flat-rate users, with a flat-rate offer at 4.99 euros per month and a 1-month trial.

competitors.name: ForfettApp
competitors.positioning: Flat-rate-focused app combining e-invoicing with storage of paid F24 forms, tax returns, INPS payments and invoices.

competitors.name: Tasse Forfettario
competitors.positioning: Independent, unofficial app that calculates substitute tax and social contributions for the flat-rate regime and shows amounts and due dates.

competitors.name: Fiscozen
competitors.positioning: Online accountant subscription for flat-rate freelancers. It includes a dedicated accountant, unlimited e-invoices, expense management and F24 handling. It is an alternative for people who want tax handled for them. Flat-rate plan from 49.90 euros per month or 499 euros per year.

competitors.name: Accountant-provided software
competitors.positioning: Invoicing software often included in the accountant's fee. It is a competitor and also a possible distribution channel for rivals.

customer_needs: Understanding how much tax they will owe: 58% of flat-rate freelancers without an invoicing app say they do not understand it [S4]
A way to meet the mandatory e-invoicing obligation through the SdI, in force for all flat-rate freelancers since 1 January 2024 [S2, S17]
Paying tax instalments (F24) from the app: 41% of the 250 beta users asked for it [S1]
Low-cost or free tools: non-app users mostly use free tax agency tools or ask their accountant [S4]; the average price paid for an invoicing app is 7.20 euros per month [S3]
Clear tax amounts and due dates for substitute tax and contributions, as offered by flat-rate tax apps [S13]
Storage of F24 payments, tax returns and INPS payments alongside invoices [S12]
Having tax handled by a dedicated professional, which some users choose despite a much higher price [S11]
Involving the accountant in the workflow, since accountants are often the source of invoicing software [S5]

segments.label: Flat-rate freelancers without an app
segments.description: Flat-rate freelancers who do not use an invoicing app yet. Purchase intent is 23% at 9 euros per month [S4]. They mostly use free tax agency tools or ask their accountant, and 58% say they do not understand how much tax they will owe [S4]. They have the highest stated intent of the four groups.
needs: Understand how much tax they will owe
Low price compared with free tools
Paying F24 from the app (requested by 41% of beta users, S1)

segments.label: Flat-rate freelancers already using an app
segments.description: Flat-rate freelancers who already use an invoicing app. Purchase intent is 9% at 9 euros per month [S4]. They would have to switch from a competitor, many of which cost less than 9 euros per month [S6, S9, S10].
needs: Reason to switch from their current app
Tax estimate and F24 features, which some flat-rate apps already offer

segments.label: Ordinary-regime freelancers with an accountant
segments.description: Freelancers in the ordinary regime who work with an accountant. Purchase intent is 6% at 9 euros per month, the lowest of the four groups [S4]. Fakturo's tax estimate is built for the flat-rate regime [S1].
needs: Export of data for the accountant

segments.label: Single-owner craft businesses (artigiani)
segments.description: Craft businesses with one owner. Purchase intent is 11% at 9 euros per month [S4].
needs: Tax clarity (not confirmed by any source for this group)

data_quality_notes: Conflict on Fatture in Cloud prices: the document gives 4 to 30 euros per month [S5]. The web gives 4 euros per month only as a first-year offer for new flat-rate customers, rising to 8 euros per month, and plans up to 51 euros per month [S6, S7]. The 4 euros figure is a promotion, so the real comparison with Fakturo's 9 euros is closer to 8 euros after year one.

Conflict on the Agenzia delle Entrate tool: the document says basic invoicing with no tax estimate [S5]. The agency's page shows the FatturAE app can also transmit invoices to the SdI [S14]. No tax estimate was found in it, but this was not checked in depth.

Fakturo's tax-estimate feature is not unique: ForfettApp and Tasse Forfettario already cover tax calculation and F24 storage [S12, S13]. The document does not say what competitors do on tax estimates or F24, and the F24 payment feature is missing from Fakturo.

No prices were found for ForfettApp, Tasse Forfettario, accountant-provided software or the 'other freelance apps' (5 to 12 euros per month, unnamed, S5), so their price level is unknown or unsupported by named sources.

The market-size and purchase-intent figures come only from the document, which cites fictional sources (Osservatorio DigitalWork 2025 and Freelance Barometer 2025) [S3, S4]. No independent market-size or growth figure was found. The MEF data cover only new registrations, not the stock of flat-rate freelancers.
Intent was measured for the 9 euros price only, so there is no evidence on demand at a lower price. Stated intent is not actual conversion.

The document does not say whether the four groups overlap. The two flat-rate groups sum to 1.9M and the flat-rate plus ordinary groups to 3.4M [S3, S4]. The 0.9M artigiani are not shown to be separate from these. It also does not say whether the flat-rate tax estimate works for artigiani or for ordinary-regime users.

The 250-user beta (68% active after 3 months, 4.4/5 rating, 41% asking for F24 [S1]) is a small sample, and no churn figure was derived from it. The Polish monthly cancellation rate of 4% is not directly comparable with the Italian goal of under 3% [S2].

Several web sources are secondary comparison or SEO pages that may carry affiliate content (promarketer.it, softwaresemplice.it, Shopify, Qonto). They were used for context, and the official pages (fattureincloud.it, agenziaentrate.gov.it, finanze.gov.it) are stronger. Prices are dated 2026, while launch is planned for January 2027, so competitor prices may change.

The price levels (low, mid, premium) are my assumptions from the cited prices, since no source gives a market price scale. The mid label for Fatture in Cloud reflects 4 to 8 euros per month for flat-rate users but higher prices on other plans.

The document says two professional associations are in talks, against a goal of three in the first year. No web research was done on associations, so there is no evidence on them. The target segment, positioning, final price and channel plan are open in the document, so the segments are presented without a recommendation.

sources.reference: Company document, section 3 (Why Italy, and launch goals)

strategy.target_description: Flat-rate (regime forfettario) freelancers in Italy who do not yet use an invoicing app. They rely on the free Agenzia delle Entrate tools or on their accountant, and many do not understand how much tax they will owe. They must send e-invoices through the SdI.
strategy.positioning_statement: For flat-rate freelancers who still invoice with free tools or through their accountant, Fakturo is the simple invoicing app that sends compliant e-invoices to the SdI and shows, with every invoice, how much tax they will owe. It goes beyond basic free invoicing. It is cheaper and simpler than an online accountant service such as Fiscozen, and it keeps the accountant in the loop through a ready export. It does not claim a unique tax estimate, because other flat-rate apps offer one, and it does not mention F24 payment, which is not yet available.
strategy.value_proposition: Know at every moment how much tax you will owe, while invoicing in the SdI-compliant format, from one simple app, with receipt photos and an export ready for your accountant.
strategy.pricing_direction: Do not price above the market without a reason: at 9 euros per month Fakturo is above the 4 to 8 euros per month of Fatture in Cloud for flat-rate users (4 in year one, then 8) and the roughly 5 euros of other apps, and above the 7.20 euros average paid [S3, S6, S10]. The free Agenzia tools are the real alternative for this segment, so the price must feel small. Recommendation: lead with the annual plan at 90 euros (7.50 euros per month equivalent, close to the 7.20 average and below the leader's post-promotion price), and test a monthly price below 9 euros during the 30-day-trial launch. Do not try to match the 4-euro first-year promotion. Intent data exist only at 9 euros [S4], so the final decision should rest on a launch price test. Whether competitor prices include VAT must be checked, because several are quoted excluding it.
strategy.rationale: SEG1 is the best primary target on size, interest, competition and fit with the goals. Size: 1.06M freelancers, the second-largest group after SEG3 at 1.5M, and larger than SEG2 (0.84M) and SEG4 (0.9M) [S4]. Interest: 23% purchase intent at 9 euros, against 9% for SEG2, 6% for SEG3 and 11% for SEG4 [S4]. Rough arithmetic on stated intent gives about 244,000 people in SEG1, against about 76,000 in SEG2, 90,000 in SEG3 and 99,000 in SEG4. Stated intent is not conversion, and the groups may overlap [S4]. The goal of 12,000 paying customers in 24 months is about 1.1% of SEG1, which is realistic. SEG3 is large but has the lowest intent, and Fakturo's tax estimate is built for the flat-rate regime [S1]. SEG4 has no evidence of tax needs [S4]. SEG2 must be won away from cheaper apps, many under 9 euros, and some already have tax and F24 features [S6, S9, S10, S12, S13]. Competition is lighter in SEG1: these users mostly use free tools or ask their accountant [S4, S14], and 58% do not understand how much tax they will owe, which matches Fakturo's tax estimate [S1, S4]. The need is lasting: e-invoicing has been mandatory for all flat-rate freelancers since 1 January 2024 [S2, S17], and new flat-rate registrations are steady, 242,529 in 2025 [S15]. Positioning risks: the tax estimate is not unique [S12, S13], the F24 payment feature that 41% of beta users asked for is missing [S1], and whether the Agenzia tool has a tax estimate was not checked in depth [S14]. For that reason the message is tax clarity inside simple invoicing, with no claim of a unique feature. The beta results (68% active after 3 months, 4.4 out of 5, 250 users) are a small sample and are used only as supporting proof. They are not used as a churn forecast, and the goal of under 3% cancellations is not proven [S1]. Channels: associations serve the goal of 3 partnerships, with two already in talks. Their size is unknown, so their reach is an assumption. Accountants are a common source of invoicing software and also a gateway that rivals use [S5], and the accountant export is a Fakturo feature [S1]. Search content on flat-rate taxes reaches people who do not understand their tax. LinkedIn and Instagram are assumed to reach freelancers, and the analysis has no channel figures for them, so they should be tested. The trial with referral lowers the barrier against free tools. The annual plan helps retention.

strategy.target_description: Freelancers in Italy under the ordinary tax regime who work with an accountant (commercialista). They need to invoice, track expenses and hand clean data to their accountant. This is the largest segment of the analysis, 1.5M freelancers.
strategy.positioning_statement: For ordinary-regime freelancers who work with an accountant, Fakturo is the invoicing app that makes the accountant's work easier: you create e-invoices, photograph receipts as you go, track expenses, and send the accountant a ready export. Unlike the invoicing software that is often bundled in an accountant's fee, you choose and control the app yourself while the accountant stays in the workflow. Unlike the broad Fatture in Cloud range, which has plans from 4 to 51 euros per month, Fakturo is a focused tool for invoices, receipts and the accountant export. The tax estimate is not part of the claim, because it is built for the flat-rate regime, and F24 payment is not mentioned because it is not yet available.
strategy.value_proposition: Invoices, receipts and expenses in one app, with an export that is ready for your accountant, so there is less manual work at tax time. Proof to use carefully: in the Italian beta, 68% of 250 users were still active after 3 months and rated the app 4.4 out of 5. The beta was not split by tax regime, so it should be presented as general proof of use.
strategy.pricing_direction: Competitor prices for this segment are only partly known. Fatture in Cloud ranges from 4 to 30 euros per month in the document and up to 51 euros on the web, and its flat-rate plan goes from 4 to 8 euros per month. The plan that fits ordinary-regime freelancers has no price in the analysis. Accountant-provided software is often included in the accountant's fee, with no price known [S5, S6, S7]. Recommendation: keep 9 euros per month and 90 euros per year as the starting point, and lead with the annual plan (7.50 euros per month equivalent), because the 4-euro offer is a first-year promotion for flat-rate customers and does not apply as a benchmark here. Before the final decision, check the price of Fatture in Cloud's ordinary-regime plan and whether quoted prices include VAT. Purchase intent was measured only at 9 euros [S4], so a lower price should be tested during the 30-day free trial rather than assumed. The trial is part of the offer, not a channel.
strategy.rationale: Feedback applied: the target is now SEG3, the only segment larger than the previous target SEG1, and the positioning, price, channels and proof were reworked for it. This also fixes the earlier warnings: the differentiator is now stated (receipt capture, expense tracking and accountant export together), the positioning is no longer based on Fiscozen, associations no longer carry the volume, and the trial is moved from channels to the offer. Size: SEG3 has 1.5M freelancers, against 1.06M for SEG1, 0.9M for SEG4 and 0.84M for SEG2 [S4]. Interest: intent is only 6% at 9 euros, the lowest of the four groups, against 23% for SEG1, 11% for SEG4 and 9% for SEG2 [S4]. Rough arithmetic on stated intent gives about 90,000 people in SEG3, against about 244,000 in SEG1. The goal of 12,000 paying customers in 24 months is 0.8% of SEG3, or about 13% of the people who state intent, versus about 5% of SEG1's stated-intent pool. Stated intent is not conversion and the groups may overlap [S4]. RISK: this choice follows the company's request for a bigger segment and goes against the evidence, which favoured SEG1 on intent. Fakturo's tax estimate is built for the flat-rate regime [S1], and the analysis does not say whether it works for ordinary-regime users, so the strongest feature of the product cannot be claimed here. Competition: accountant-provided software is a competitor, and also a distribution gateway for rivals [S5]. Fatture in Cloud is the leader with a wide range [S6]. The needs of SEG3 (data export, expense tracking, compatibility with the accountant's workflow) match features Fakturo has [S1, S4]. Fakturo's tax estimate is not unique anyway [S12, S13], so it is not used as an edge. It is an assumption that the beta users resemble SEG3, as the beta was not split by regime. The beta is a small sample and gives no churn figure, so the goal of under 3% cancellations is not proven [S1]. Channels: accountants and search carry the volume, since the accountant is the key relationship for this segment and the accountant export is a Fakturo feature [S1, S5]. Search content reaches freelancers comparing invoicing tools. Professional associations serve the goal of 3 partnerships in the first year, and the analysis notes two already in talks, but there is no information about their size or whether their members are ordinary-regime freelancers. Their reach is therefore an assumption and they are not counted on for volume until member numbers are known. LinkedIn leads among social channels for reaching professionals, as an assumption with no channel figures in the analysis, so it should be tested. Instagram is dropped to keep one message per channel. Data quality: market-size and intent figures come only from the company document [S3, S4]. The Agenzia delle Entrate free tools can send e-invoices to the SdI [S14], so the pitch against them is the accountant workflow and expense tracking, not invoicing alone.

strategy.target_description: Flat-rate (regime forfettario) freelancers in Italy who do not yet use an invoicing app. Today they mostly use the free Agenzia delle Entrate tools or ask their accountant. Many do not understand how much tax they will owe. The segment has 1.06M freelancers.
strategy.positioning_statement: For flat-rate freelancers who still invoice with free tools or through their accountant, Fakturo is the low-cost invoicing app that also shows how much tax they will owe. It is priced below the market average and below what Fatture in Cloud charges after its first-year promotion. It has a single, stable price with no jump after the first year. It is not the cheapest option on the market: the Agenzia delle Entrate tools are free and some apps start near 1 to 5 euros per month. The pitch is therefore 'a small, fair monthly cost for compliant e-invoices plus a tax estimate updated with every invoice'. It avoids claims that the analysis does not support: it does not say Fakturo is unique on tax estimates (ForfettApp and Tasse Forfettario offer them), it does not mention F24 payment (not yet available) and it does not claim the lowest price.
strategy.value_proposition: Compliant e-invoices sent to the SdI and a tax estimate that updates with every invoice, so you know what you will owe, for a lower monthly price than the leader's post-promotion rate and the market average. Receipt photos and an accountant export are included. Proof, to be used carefully: in the Italian beta, 68% of 250 users were still active after 3 months and rated the app 4.4 out of 5. The sample is small and the beta was not split by tax regime.
strategy.pricing_direction: Lower than the planned 9 euros per month, as the feedback asks for a cheaper positioning. Competitor reference points: the average price paid by flat-rate app users is 7.20 euros per month [S3]. Fatture in Cloud's flat-rate plan is 4 euros per month in year one and 8 euros afterwards [S6]. FatturaElettronica APP is 4.99 euros per month [S10]. Aruba starts at 1 euro + VAT for 3 months [S8, S9]. Fiscozen is 49.90 euros per month [S11], and the Agenzia delle Entrate tools are free [S14]. Recommendation: launch below 7.20 euros per month so that the 'cheaper than average and than the leader after year one' claim holds. As an assumption to be tested, try a range of roughly 5 to 7 euros per month, with an annual plan priced at a discount to the monthly one, and keep the 30-day free trial as part of the offer, not as a channel. Do not try to beat the 4-euro promotion or the free tools on price. Intent was measured only at 9 euros [S4], so there is no evidence yet on demand at a lower price. Revenue per customer will fall against the 9-euro plan, and the analysis has no cost data. The company should check that a lower price still works for its margins before fixing it. Also check whether competitor prices include VAT, because several are quoted + VAT.
strategy.rationale: Feedback applied: the positioning and price are now 'cheaper': below the 7.20-euro market average [S3] and below Fatture in Cloud's 8 euros after year one [S6], not the cheapest on the market. I also moved the target from SEG3 to SEG1, because a price claim needs known competitor prices. Those are known for flat-rate users but not for ordinary-regime users, and it fixes the segment-size warning. Segments [S4]: SEG1 has 1.06M freelancers and 23% intent at 9 euros, about 244,000 people. SEG3 has 1.5M and 6%, about 90,000. SEG4 has 0.9M and 11%, about 99,000. SEG2 has 0.84M and 9%, about 76,000. These are rough products of stated figures, not forecasts, and the groups may overlap. The goal of 12,000 paying customers is about 1.1% of SEG1 and about 5% of its stated-intent pool. In SEG3 it would be about 13% of the stated-intent pool. SEG1 has the most demand, and 58% of them say they do not understand how much tax they will owe [S4]. This matches Fakturo's tax estimate and flat-rate fit [S1]. Competition: SEG1 is the least served by apps, as it has no app today [S4]. SEG2 would have to switch from cheaper apps [S6, S9, S10]. The risk: this segment's alternatives are free tools [S14], so price sensitivity is high, and the tax estimate is not unique [S12, S13]. Intent was measured at 9 euros only, so a lower price may raise conversion, but this is an assumption. This choice goes against the earlier wish for the largest segment. SEG3 stays reachable later through the accountant export, but is not the target. Cancellations: the beta gives no churn figure [S1], and a lower price does not by itself guarantee under 3%, so that goal is not proven. Channels: non-app users use free tools or ask their accountant [S4]. Search ads and SEO content catch freelancers who look up e-invoicing and tax questions, with the message 'know your tax and invoice for a small fixed price'. Comparison and review sites carry the price message, since the web sources comparing prices are of this type [S8, S9, S10]. They may carry affiliate content, so the cost should be checked. Accountants are an influence on non-users [S4, S5], but accountant-provided software is also a competitor [S5], so the message there is the export and the accountant stays in the workflow. Professional associations serve the goal of 3 partnerships in the first year. Two are reportedly in talks, but their size and member profile are unknown, so they are not counted on for volume. The channel reach is an assumption, as the analysis has no channel figures. Data quality: market-size and intent figures come only from the company document [S3, S4]. Prices are dated 2026 and launch is planned for January 2027, so they may change.

campaign.concept: "Il conto giusto": every invoice a flat-rate freelancer sends also updates a running tax estimate, so a small, fixed monthly cost buys two things at once, compliant e-invoices and clarity on what they will owe. The campaign turns the anxious question "quanto pagherò di tasse?" into a calm, everyday habit, and presents Fakturo as the fair, honest alternative to free tools and to apps whose price jumps after year one. It expresses the positioning directly: low-cost invoicing that also shows the tax, with one stable price.
campaign.tagline: Fatture in regola, tasse chiare, prezzo giusto.

key_messages.headline: Fatture elettroniche + stima delle tasse, in un'unica app
key_messages.body: Sei in regime forfettario? Fakturo crea la fattura elettronica, la invia allo SdI e aggiorna la stima delle tasse a ogni fattura. Un piccolo costo mensile, prezzo fisso, 30 giorni di prova gratuita.

key_messages.headline: Quante tasse pagherai in forfettario? Guarda la stima aggiornata
key_messages.body: Ogni nuova fattura aggiorna la stima di quanto dovrai. Scopri come funziona la guida e prova Fakturo gratis per 30 giorni.

key_messages.headline: Fakturo: un prezzo unico, senza aumenti dopo il primo anno
key_messages.body: Fatture elettroniche inviate allo SdI, stima delle tasse per il regime forfettario aggiornata a ogni fattura, foto degli scontrini ed export per il commercialista. Un piccolo costo mensile equo, sempre lo stesso. Prova gratuita di 30 giorni.

key_messages.headline: Nella beta italiana, 68% ancora attivo dopo 3 mesi
key_messages.body: Su 250 utenti della beta in Italia, il 68% usava ancora Fakturo dopo 3 mesi e la valutazione media è stata 4,4 su 5. Provalo con 30 giorni gratuiti.

key_messages.headline: Il tuo cliente fattura in regola. Tu ricevi tutto con un export.
key_messages.body: Con Fakturo i clienti in regime forfettario emettono fatture elettroniche, fotografano gli scontrini e ti inviano i dati con l'export per il commercialista. Tu resti al centro del lavoro, con documenti più ordinati.

key_messages.headline: Per le partite IVA in forfettario: fatture in regola e tasse chiare
key_messages.body: Fakturo è l'app pensata per chi è in regime forfettario: fattura elettronica verso lo SdI, stima delle tasse aggiornata a ogni fattura, prezzo fisso senza salti dopo il primo anno. Scopri come provarla per 30 giorni gratuiti.

content_ideas: Google search ad set around queries such as 'fattura elettronica forfettario' and 'quante tasse pago in forfettario', all pointing to a landing page with the 30-day free trial.
SEO guide series in Italian: 'Fattura elettronica per il regime forfettario, passo per passo' and 'Come leggere la tua stima delle tasse', each with a short product demo.
Fakturo profile and listing pages on Italian price-comparison and software review sites, with a clear single-price panel and the beta figures (250 users, 68% active after 3 months, 4.4/5).
Short screen-capture video: create an invoice, see the tax estimate move, in under 60 seconds, for search landing pages and review-site listings.
One-page leaflet and email template for commercialisti to share with flat-rate clients, explaining the accountant export and the receipt photo capture.
Co-branded webinar proposal for professional associations: 'E-invoicing and tax estimate for flat-rate freelancers', with a live demo and Q&A.
Printable member-information sheet for professional associations, in Italian, with a QR code to the free-trial page.
Interactive landing-page widget where a visitor enters a sample invoice amount and sees how the tax estimate view works.
campaign.visual_direction: Clean, calm and trustworthy, with a friendly Italian feel. Palette: deep ink blue for trust, warm off-white background, and one bright accent (a fresh green or amber) to highlight the tax estimate figure. Imagery: real freelancers (designers, photographers, consultants, tradespeople) working in small studios or cafés, shot in natural light, with a phone or laptop showing the app. Key visual: a large invoice card with a smaller live "stima tasse" counter ticking up beside it, repeated across all formats. Typography: modern rounded sans-serif, big numerals, short sentences. Packaging and UI cues: the app icon is a simple "F" on a blue square; screenshots show the invoice screen and the tax estimate screen side by side; a badge reading "30 giorni gratis" and "Prezzo fisso" on ads and landing pages. For commercialisti and associations, a more sober version of the same look: more white space, fewer photos, clear feature list.
